flagship.headline: Bob Dylan records All Along the Watchtower in Nashville
flagship.summary_line_1: Bob Dylan recorded All Along the Watchtower at Columbia Studio A in Nashville on November 6, 1967, for his album John Wesley Harding, per Wikipedia.
flagship.summary_line_2: Charlie McCoy played bass and Kenneth Buttrey played drums, and the clip below is the official audio.

events.headline: The Monkees' film Head premieres in New York City
events.summary_line_1: The Monkees film Head had its New York City premiere on November 6, 1968, per the AFI Catalog.
events.summary_line_2: Bob Rafelson directed it and Jack Nicholson co-wrote it, it did poorly at the box office, and the clip below is Porpoise Song, the film's theme.

events.headline: Bob Dylan records All Along the Watchtower in Nashville
events.summary_line_1: Bob Dylan recorded All Along the Watchtower at Columbia Studio A in Nashville on November 6, 1967, for his album John Wesley Harding, per Wikipedia.
events.summary_line_2: Charlie McCoy played bass and Kenneth Buttrey played drums, and the clip below is the official audio.

events.headline: Guitarist Paul Gilbert is born in Carbondale, Illinois
events.summary_line_1: Paul Gilbert was born in Carbondale, Illinois on November 6, 1966, per Wikipedia.
events.summary_line_2: He went on to play in Racer X and co-found Mr. Big, and the clip below is the Mr. Big song To Be With You.

events.headline: The Rolling Stones hit No. 1 with Get Off of My Cloud
events.summary_line_1: The Rolling Stones topped the Billboard Hot 100 on the chart dated November 6, 1965, with Get Off of My Cloud, for two weeks, per Wikipedia.
events.summary_line_2: It followed (I Can't Get No) Satisfaction as their second American No. 1, and the clip below is the single.

events.headline: Jazz pianist Clarence Williams dies in Queens
events.summary_line_1: Clarence Williams, the pianist, songwriter and producer born in Plaquemine, Louisiana, died in Queens, New York on November 6, 1965, per Wikipedia.
events.summary_line_2: He led Clarence Williams' Blue Five, and the clip below is the band playing Mean Blues.

events.headline: The Beatles play two shows at the Gaumont in Southampton
events.summary_line_1: The Beatles played two shows at the Gaumont Cinema in Southampton on November 6, 1964, at 6.15pm and 8.40pm, with Mary Wells on the bill, per the Beatles Bible.
events.summary_line_2: It was the 23rd date of their autumn British tour and their third and final Southampton concert, and the clip below is the title song of their 1964 film A Hard Day's Night.

events.headline: Christian Death founder Rozz Williams is born
events.summary_line_1: Rozz Williams, who founded Christian Death, was born on November 6, 1963, per Rolling Stone.
events.summary_line_2: He was 16 when Christian Death recorded its debut album Only Theatre of Pain, and the clip below is its opening track, Cavity - First Communion.

events.headline: The Beatles play the Star-Club in Hamburg
events.summary_line_1: The Beatles played the Star-Club in Hamburg on November 6, 1962, the sixth show of a 14-night second residency that ran from November 1 to 14, per the Paul McCartney Project.
events.summary_line_2: Love Me Do had come out a month earlier, and the clip below is that single.

events.headline: Jimmy Dean hits No. 1 with Big Bad John
events.summary_line_1: Jimmy Dean topped the Billboard Hot 100 on the chart dated November 6, 1961, with Big Bad John, for five weeks, per the list of 1961 Hot 100 number ones.
events.summary_line_2: It was his only Hot 100 No. 1 and earned him a Grammy for best country and western recording, and the clip below is the single.
